interest: Shows 1946-48 occupation-era shift from trade embargo to patent restoration and tech transfer, like vitamin-extraction equipment for Japan.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
overview: This file (decimal file 894.54211, File 1653) from the U.S. State Department's central decimal files covers diplomatic and administrative correspondence from 1946 and 1948 concerning the postwar status, restoration, and protection of American intellectual and industrial property rights in Allied-occupied Japan. The documentation centers on two primary inquiries: a March 1946 exchange initiated by international patent firm Marks & Clerk regarding the reinstatement of lapsed patents and trademarks and the safeguarding of American-owned subsidiary manufacturing plants under SCAP jurisdiction; and an August–September 1948 exchange involving Distillation Products, Inc. regarding patent protection, royalties, and commercial vetting after receiving an inquiry from a Japanese chemical firm (Matsumoto Fat, Oil, & Chemical Man. Co. Ltd., recommended by SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section) seeking molecular distillation equipment and know-how to extract vitamins A and D from cod liver oil. Across these communications, State Department officials (including Robert P. Terrill, Roswell H. Whitman, and Raymond Vernon) clarify the transition from wartime sequestration and commercial prohibitions to Allied policies under the Far Eastern Commission and SCAP, outlining procedures for patent re-validation, war damage claims, and commercial intelligence channels.
